question: What is the general age range for adolescents according to the World Health Organization?
explanation: The World Health Organization specifically defines the adolescent period as spanning from 10 to 19 years of age. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h1)

question: Why do traditional health facilities often fail to meet the needs of teenagers?

options.A: They do not have enough medical equipment for diagnosing infections
options.B: They are only open during school hours every day
options.C: They charge too much money compared to private pharmacies
options.D: They are usually structured for adults or young children rather than teenagers

explanation: Standard clinics are typically designed for adults or young children, which makes the environment intimidating for adolescents seeking care. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h1)

question: What does the accessibility principle mean in youth-friendly health services?

options.A: Staff members must speak at least three local languages fluently
options.B: Services must be affordable, conveniently located, and open at suitable times
options.C: Healthcare workers must visit every school in the community monthly
options.D: Clinics must provide free medications for all chronic illnesses

explanation: Accessibility ensures that cost, location, and operating hours do not prevent young people from getting the care they need. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h2)

question: A clinic ensures that all adolescents receive care regardless of their financial status or background. Which core principle does this practice demonstrate?
explanation: Equitability means treating all young clients fairly without discrimination based on status, gender, or ability to pay. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h2)

question: Which nutritional issue is especially common during the rapid physical growth of adolescence?
explanation: Rapid growth and poor dietary habits make adolescents, especially young females, very prone to developing anaemia. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h3)

question: What is a common misconception about the health status of adolescents?

options.A: They are naturally healthy and rarely need medical attention
options.B: They have complete immunity against sexually transmitted infections
options.C: They never experience emotional or mental health challenges
options.D: They suffer from chronic heart conditions more than older adults

explanation: Many people mistakenly assume teenagers do not need healthcare because they look strong, ignoring important preventive and mental health needs. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to healthcare access for youths in Nigeria?

options.A: Financial constraints due to out-of-pocket payments
options.B: Free medical services available at every clinic
options.D: Fear of breaking confidentiality laws or parental rules

explanation: Free medical services are rare, and financial cost is actually one of the biggest barriers young people face in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h4)

question: Why do laws requiring parental consent for minor treatments often harm adolescent health?

options.A: They prevent nurses from administering routine childhood immunizations
options.B: They discourage adolescents from seeking care for sensitive issues out of fear
options.C: They cause doctors to refuse treatment for routine malaria and fevers
options.D: They make clinic waiting times much longer for everyone in the community

explanation: When teens know their parents must be informed, they often avoid seeking vital care for reproductive health or substance use. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h4)

question: What does providing integrated services mean in an adolescent clinic?

options.A: Requiring both parents to attend every medical consultation with the teen
options.B: Using traditional medicine alongside modern pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: Offering multiple health services like reproductive and mental care under one roof
options.D: Combining adult and adolescent patients in the same waiting room

explanation: Integrated services mean a young person can access different types of healthcare in a single convenient location. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h5)

question: Why is community outreach considered a key component of youth-friendly health services?

options.A: It replaces the need for clinical staff inside the actual health facility
options.B: It ensures that the government provides free drugs to every household
options.C: It helps parents and community leaders understand and support the clinic
options.D: It allows nurses to diagnose community illnesses without laboratory tests

explanation: Outreach builds trust and reduces community resistance by educating adults about the importance of youth health services. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h5)

question: What is the primary position of the nurse in adolescent healthcare delivery?

options.B: Hospital administrator who manages the budget
options.C: Strict disciplinarian who enforces clinic rules
options.D: Laboratory technician who runs blood tests

explanation: Nurses are usually the first health professionals young clients interact with, acting as counselors and guides. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h6)

question: A nurse notices that teenage patients look nervous and hesitant when entering the consultation room. What immediate action should the nurse take?

options.A: Refuse to examine the patient until an older family member arrives
options.B: Scold the teenager for being afraid of a routine medical checkup
options.C: Use a warm tone and a welcoming posture to help put the teen at ease
options.D: Insist that a security guard stays inside the room during the interview

explanation: A welcoming attitude and friendly demeanor help break down anxiety and build trust with young clients. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h6)

question: What is considered the absolute cornerstone of youth-friendly healthcare?
explanation: Guarantees of privacy and confidentiality are essential to make young people feel safe enough to share personal health details. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h7)

question: When is it legally and ethically necessary for a nurse to break adolescent confidentiality?

options.A: Whenever the clinic manager requests a routine attendance report
options.B: When the adolescent refuses to take prescribed multivitamin tablets
options.C: When the teenager is at risk of suicide or severe harm
options.D: Whenever a parent asks about the teen's school grades

explanation: Safety comes first; if a young person is suicidal or facing severe danger, confidentiality must be broken to protect them. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h7)

question: Why is community engagement important for adolescent health programs?

options.A: It forces all teenagers in the neighborhood to visit the hospital daily
options.B: It gives the nursing staff extra financial bonuses from the local government
options.C: It eliminates the need for any trained medical personnel in the clinic
options.D: It builds local ownership and ensures long-term support for sensitive health topics

explanation: Involving community leaders and parents prevents resistance and builds strong local backing for youth programs. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h8)

question: How do patient satisfaction surveys and attendance logs help an adolescent health clinic?

options.A: They prove to the government that no teenagers are sick in the area
options.B: They guarantee that the clinic will receive international funding
options.C: They allow the team to identify gaps and improve services over time
options.D: They replace the need for physical examinations during consultations

explanation: Tracking data and feedback helps clinics see what is working well and where changes are needed to better serve youths. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h8)
